**The meaning of the verse**
﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِّن قَوْمٍ عَسَىٰ أَن يَكُونُوا خَيْرًا مِّنْهُمْ﴾
O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law: let no believing people mock other believing people; perhaps those who are mocked are better than those who mock. And let no believing women mock other believing women; perhaps those who are mocked are better than those who mock. And do not find fault with one another, and do not call one another by nicknames they dislike. How evil is the description and name of wickedness — which is mocking, finding fault and calling by nicknames — after you have entered Islam and understood it. And whoever does not repent of this mocking, fault-finding, name-calling and wickedness, those are the ones who have wronged themselves by committing these forbidden things.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. What did Fahd use to do when Hilal spoke? And how was Hilal when he went back home?
2. When the boys got lost in the desert, who brought them back to the village? And what did Fahd say to his father?
3. Hilal sometimes laughed along with them, so was that harmless joking? (No; allowed joking is when everyone laughs and no one is hurt. As for copying the way someone talks or calling them by a nickname they dislike, that is mocking, which Allah has forbidden, even if the person laughs along out of shyness.)

**This week's exercise**
Every day your child mentions something good that someone around them does well (a brother or sister, a classmate, or a neighbour) that others have not noticed. And this week the family agrees that no one at home calls anyone by a nickname they dislike.
